title.narrative: Science-policy nexus strengthened through management of social transformation

description.narrative:
Situated within the strategic framework of the MOST Programme, aimed at bridging knowledge-policy gap, this activity is divided into two distinct tracks, with both contributing to the implementation of all three performance indicators (3.1 & 3.2 for disabilities and 3.3 for GHA). The first track focuses on disabilities inclusion, specifically strengthening capacities of existing institutions and structures, and enhancing coordination mechanisms to advance inclusion of persons with disabilities at national and subnational levels including cities and municipalities of Member States in Southern Africa. To complement this action, sub-activities will be further developed to generate additional data and analyses, to inform policy and legislative reforms in Member States, building on previous achievements, in particular, in Zimbabwe and Eswatini, and upscaling in additional countries in the region.
The second axis focuses on implementation of Priority Africa flagship programme on General History of Africa, with two main actions pursued as follows: first, operationalization of UNITWIN Network on General History of Africa (GHA) as a key knowledge and strategic partner on the relevance of history to manage social transformations, and second, mainstreaming Southern Africa Liberation History (SALH) into GHA, and specifically, in partnership with Southern Africa Development Community (SADC), develop a regional framework on SALH, with three pillars (education curriculum integration and reform, youth-led knowledge generation and production, and documentary heritage), anchored across key sectors in Member States.
